original_question: Does every Kropina metric on a closed manifold have a closed geodesic?
target_in_paper: Question 2.5.1 in §2.5, "Kropina metrics with nonintegrable distribution": "Does every Kropina metric on a closed manifold have a closed geodesic?" ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper: it matches Question 2.5.1 almost verbatim and asks exactly about the existence of a closed geodesic for every Kropina metric on a closed manifold. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the question should specify the paper's Kropina setup: a Riemannian metric g together with a nowhere-vanishing 1-form ω, with the Kropina metric written in the paper as F = g/ω. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

The scope is not arbitrary Kropina data: §2.5 is explicitly about "Kropina metrics with nonintegrable distribution," so the intended hypothesis is that the hyperplane distribution ker ω is nonintegrable. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

The paper also notes that this is not a Finsler metric in the usual sense, because F is not defined on ker ω; nevertheless it is one-homogeneous and strictly convex where defined. Those domain and regularity facts are implicit in the draft. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
Section 1 fixes the global convention that M is connected, so a maximally explicit stand-alone version should say "closed connected manifold." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

Immediately after the question, the paper states that if π1(M) is nontrivial then the answer is already positive by essentially the Riemannian argument, so the genuinely open content is the simply connected case. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

No ambient ring/field, degree, nilpotency, or "for all sufficiently large m" clauses are involved here; the missing details are geometric definitions and hypotheses rather than algebraic or asymptotic parameters. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
refined_question: Let M be a closed connected manifold, let g be a Riemannian metric on M, and let ω be a nowhere-vanishing 1-form whose kernel distribution ker ω is nonintegrable. For the associated Kropina metric F = g/ω, defined away from ker ω and viewed there as a one-homogeneous strictly convex function, must there exist a closed geodesic on M? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
equivalent_formulation: Since the paper states that the answer is positive whenever π1(M) is nontrivial, an equivalent formulation of the open part is: if M is a closed simply connected manifold, does every Kropina metric of the above type admit a closed geodesic? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
justification: This draft clearly targets the later Kropina section, not the earlier conjectures: the exact paper item is Question 2.5.1 in §2.5. The draft already captures the official existence problem, but to make it sharp and self-contained one must import the section's local notation and hypotheses: Kropina data come from g and ω, the metric is undefined on ker ω, the section is framed by nonintegrability of ker ω, and the post-question remark shows that the only genuinely open case is when M is simply connected. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
